name: Xero
summary: Cloud accounting for small business: bank reconciliation, invoicing, bills and reporting.
best_for: small businesses whose bookkeeper or accountant already works in Xero — the ecosystem and the bank feeds are the real product, and the monthly price is small against what the reconciliation time costs
skip_if: you invoice a handful of clients and reconcile by hand — the entry tier at $25 after the promo is buying automation you may not need yet, and simpler invoicing tools cost less
honest_knock: Read the second number, not the first. Every plan on that page is 90% off for six months, and the price that governs the rest of your first year is ten times what the button says: $25, $55 and $90. That is not hidden — it is printed right there — but it is printed smaller, and the plan people pick on the strength of $2.50 a month is the one that becomes $25. Then read the notice further down, because it undercuts even that: Xero says subscription prices are increasing from 1 October 2026, the day after the offer closes, without printing the new rates. So month seven costs $25 or more, and the page will not tell you which. The second thing to check is the entry tier's ceiling: Early is 20 invoices and 5 bills a month, the limit counts approving as well as sending, and connected apps can eat into it on your behalf — which makes Growing at $55 the realistic starting price for anyone billing through other software. And check which country's page you are on, because Xero's tiers and prices differ by market.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on their own US pricing page) Every headline price is still a promotion: 'Get 90% off your plan for your first 6 months when you buy by 30 September 2026'. Early is $2.50 a month for the first six months and then $25. Growing is $5.50 and then $55. Established is $9 and then $90. New on this reading: the same page carries a notice that Xero subscription prices are increasing from 1 October 2026 — the day after the offer closes — and does not print the new rates. Also new: the tier limits. Early is capped at 20 invoices and 5 bills a month, and the footnote states the invoice limit counts both approving and sending, and that transactions initiated by app partners may automatically contribute to it. Multi-currency and project tracking remain on Established only. The offer terms restrict it to new US customers buying their first organisation with code DC90626308US, cover the base subscription only, and auto-renew monthly at the regular price. Optional add-ons: Inventory Plus (no price shown, and excluded on Early) and Xero Payroll powered by Gusto at $36 a month plus $6 per employee or contractor, which the discount does not cover. Standard ACH bill payments are included; fees apply for other methods, same-day ACH and cross-border. Prices are USD and exclude tax; a downgrade is only allowed one month after an upgrade. Xero prices differently by country.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Open-source local server connecting an LLM to Xero accounting data, part of an AI toolkit that also ships a CLI and OpenAI Agents SDK and LangChain integrations. A hosted remote server exists too, but only as a closed beta under separate terms.
vendor_mcp.plan: Not stated for the open-source server. The remote beta's own terms are blunter than most: "if the Software moves out of beta phase and is released commercially, you may need to pay for use of the final commercial product."
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
